content: {"summary":"On 24 June 2025 the pgx connection pool on each payments‑api pod reached its maximum size, causing requests to wait and emit PAYAPI‑E1042, which filled the server connections observed in SHOW POOLS (cl_waiting≈30).","likely_cause":"pgx pool exhaustion – connections were held (e.g., idle‑in‑transaction) until the pool hit its max_conns, filling the server connections","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"The pool reached its max connections, causing requests to wait and log PAYAPI‑E1042","evidence_ids":["RB-010#0"],"quote":"If every connection is checked out, the request waits... we log `PAYAPI-E1042`"},{"text":"Four pods with pool_max_conns=40 can use up to 160 client connections, which can fill the server","evidence_ids":["RB-010#1"],"quote":"With 4 pods ... that's up to 160 client connections"},{"text":"Many sessions were idle in transaction, holding connections and contributing to the full pool","evidence_ids":["RB-010#3"],"quote":"Acquired connections high, but payments-db shows most of our sessions `idle in transaction`"}],"next_checks":["Query pg_stat_activity for sessions in 'idle in transaction' state","Collect a goroutine dump to identify Acquire waiters and holders","Verify DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT and pool_max_conns settings in the ConfigMap","Monitor payments_db_pool_acquired_conns and acquire_wait_seconds metrics per pod"]}
